ROOT CYCLE09: POLAR KATO INEQUALITY AND THE SINE HYPERCONTRACTIVE CURVE
Origin: root. Internal analytic candidate, conditional on the separately
audited Cycle09 full-p profile. No external/formal/priority claim.
Written after reading complexity's independently frozen signed profile and
its exposed audit of root's two-by-two all-complex dilation lead. This is
not an independent rediscovery of the signed profile. The Kato averaging and
all-complex norm derivative below were derived by root after that exposure.

1. Definitions and supplied premises

Finite faithful sigma, s=sqrt(sigma), Gamma(X)=sXs, and positive KMS QMS
generator L. Its Hilbert-Schmidt implementation is
 H=Gamma^(1/2)L Gamma^(-1/2).
The independently audited legal-noise representation supplies a sum of
 H_B(Q)={V_B,Q}/2-BQB, B=B*, V_B=2 Lyap_s^(-1)(BsB).

For arbitrary complex f and finite p>1, let A=Gamma^(1/p)f=U|A|,
 I_(a,p)^polar(f)=Gamma^(-1/a)[U|A|^(p/a)],
 Ep(f)=p/[2(p-1)] Re <I_(p',p)^polar(f),L f>_sigma.
The Cycle09 lower-profile candidate, now independently reconstructed and
under exposed audit, gives
 Ep(f)>=c_p E2(I_(2,p)^polar f),
 c_p=p sin(pi/p)/[2(p-1)].
For p2, E2(g)=<g,Lg>_sigma=Tr Q*H(Q), Q=Gamma^(1/2)g.
The polar version follows exactly from the signed-Hermitian theorem applied
to D_f=[[0,f],[f*,0]], stationary state (I2/2) tensor sigma. No positive
log-Sobolev constant for that untouched-reference generator is presumed.

Assume just the ordinary POSITIVE-input 2-LSI
 E2(g)>=alpha2 Ent2(g), g>=0,
 Ent2(g)=Z/2 D(rho||sigma),
 Z=Tr Q^2, rho=Q^2/Z, Q=Gamma^(1/2)g>=0.
We will transfer that ordinary positive LSI to arbitrary complex observables
using the elementary Kato average, not an invalid tensor-product LSI.

2. Exact Kato average for every legal noise

For arbitrary square complex Q, write Q=U|Q| and choose a unitary extension
of its polar partial isometry. Then |Q*|=U|Q|U*. For Hermitian B set
 C=|Q|^(1/2)B|Q|^(1/2),
 A0=|Q|^(1/2)U*BU|Q|^(1/2),
both Hermitian. The real Hilbert-Schmidt inequality
 Tr A0 C <= [Tr A0^2+Tr C^2]/2
proves
 Re Tr Q* B Q B
 <= [Tr |Q*| B |Q*| B + Tr |Q| B |Q| B]/2.
The drift is exactly
 Tr Q*{V,Q}/2 = Tr V(QQ*+Q*Q)/2.
It agrees with the average of the two absolute-value drift terms. Therefore
 E_H(Q)>= [E_H(|Q|)+E_H(|Q*|)]/2.
This holds termwise, hence for all finite KMS generators. It does not require
V commute with Q or any modular covariance.

ROOT-SUPPLIED POSITIVE LSI/SINE CURVE AND INDEPENDENT CP POLAR EXTENSION
Cycle09; algebra_proof_recon; Sol/max; no descendants.
This separate calculation was frozen AFTER the independent legal upper
packet and BEFORE reading root's Kato proof or any current sibling proof.
All earlier report and manifest bytes are immutable.

STATUS AND ATTRIBUTION

PASS, CONDITIONALLY on the specified universal POSITIVE-input profile.
The root-supplied positive p-LSI factor and hypercontractive ODE are exact
under the assigned/source energy and entropy conventions. An independent
CP polar-block argument extends the resulting positive-input norm bound
to all complex inputs on the original M_d without an amplified LSI or a
complex-energy profile premise. The converse from the sine curve at p0=2
to positive LSI2 follows from its derivative at zero.

The universal energy profile itself is not proved or audited here. This
file does not infer an optimal hypercontractive curve from sharpness of
the pointwise profile. Complete/amplified norm contractivity is not
asserted without corresponding amplified positive-input bounds.

Root supplied the proposed LSI factor/ODE and, later, the converse claim.
Their trace and differential calculations are independently verified
below. The CP polar-block norm extension is independently acquired here;
it does NOT use root's separate Kato averaging derivation. The latter
file is still unread at this freeze.

1. Precise conditional interface and sign convention

Let sigma>0, Tr sigma=1. Write Gamma(X)=sigma^(1/2)Xsigma^(1/2), and
Gamma^a(X)=sigma^(a/2)Xsigma^(a/2). Let P_t=exp(-tL) be UCP on M_d
and sigma stationary; L is the POSITIVE generator. KMS symmetry is as
in the independent upper packet, though the algebraic consequence below
only needs the declared profile and a legal CP semigroup.

For f>0, p>1, q=p/(p-1), use

  I_(q,p)(f)=Gamma^(-1/q)((Gamma^(1/p)f)^(p-1)),
  E_p(f)=p/[2(p-1)] <I_(q,p)(f),Lf>_sigma,
  E_2(g)=<g,Lg>_sigma.

Assume the following ONLY FOR POSITIVE inputs, for every finite p>1:

  E_p(f)>=c_p E_2(I_(2,p)f),
  c_p=p sin(pi/p)/[2(p-1)].                           (P)

Also assume positive-state LSI2 at a constant alpha2>=0:

  E_2(g)>=alpha2 Ent_2(g), for every g>0.             (LSI2+)

For rho=(Gamma^(1/2)g)^2 the root-specified/source entropy is

  Ent_2(g)=[Tr(rho log rho)-Tr(rho log sigma)
                       -(Tr rho)
